sections.label: E-scooter road and footpath measures
sections.summary: Passage asks what LTA and Traffic Police do to keep e-scooters off roads and address unsafe footpath use, noting 30 accidents, 1,700 advisories and upcoming Active Mobility Act fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the current measures taken by LTA and the Traffic Police to (i) ensure that e-scooters are not used on roads and expressways, and electric bicycles are not used on expressways and (ii) address unsafe and inconsiderate usage of e-scooters on footpaths and walkways; and (b) whether more measures will be taken to (i) abate such occurrences and (ii) enhance public awareness of the laws governing the usage of e-scooters and electric bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: There were about 30 reported accidents involving pedestrians and Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs), including e-scooters, on public paths from January to September last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Last year, LTA issued more than 1,700 advisories for unsafe riding behaviours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Offenders will also pay fines once the Active Mobility Act comes into force soon.

sections.label: Penalties for PMD offenders
sections.summary: Passage states offenders can be prosecuted, fined up to $1,000 or jailed up to three months, with composition sums rising to $300 and $500 from 15 January.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Offenders can face prosecution, be convicted and pay a fine up to $1,000, or imprisonment of up to three months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In response to the growing use of PMDs, the composition sum of $100 will be increased to $300 and $500 for offenders who ride on local and major roads, respectively, from next week, 15 January.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: If convicted, offenders face a fine of up to $2,000, or imprisonment of up to three months, or more.

sections.label: Active Mobility Advisory Panel review
sections.summary: Passage states the Active Mobility Advisory Panel will review the code of conduct for active mobility devices, including insurance, helmets and e-scooter registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I think both are reasonable and good suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I have actually asked the Active Mobility Advisory Panel chaired by my colleague, Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim, to review the code of conduct and practices governing active mobility devices (AMDs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Some of these suggestions, I am sure the panel will take into account as well, including insurance, wearing of helmets and whether we should register e-scooters.
